items.title: MongoDB修補可能導致資料庫切換節點時當機的重大漏洞
items.summary: 資料庫軟體業者MongoDB於11月10日修補資料庫伺服器重大漏洞CVE-2026-118383，CVSS嚴重性評分達9.5。

items.title: 韓國企業協作平臺DaouOffice傳遭零時差漏洞攻擊，客戶共用帳號又遭暴力破解，至少3家金融業者受駭
items.summary: 韓國企業協作平臺DaouOffice近期接連傳出不同類型的資安事件，服務供應商Daou Technology（다우기술）在11月先後發布兩則安全公告，分別說明產品存取控制漏洞遭利用的攻擊事故，以及企業共用帳號遭暴力破解的情況，強調兩起事故原因不同。值得注意的是，事件影響已陸續浮現，先前的存取控制漏洞攻擊事件波及韓國加密貨幣交易所Bithumb及漢陽證券，後續的帳號暴力破解事件則涉及另一家加密貨幣交易所Flybit，3家金融業者均傳出客戶或員工個資外洩。 從事件揭露的時間來看，DaouOffice相關資安事故先後由受影響企業公布，服務供應商Daou Technology隨後才發布公開說明。

items.title: 微軟Windows本機AI模型將改用Aion Instruct，輸入上下文上限擴大逾9倍
items.summary: 微軟公布Windows裝置端語言模型更替計畫，將以Aion Instruct取代Phi Silica，預計11月20日起先向參與Windows Insider計畫的Copilot+ PC分階段推送，2027年1月下旬擴大至符合硬體條件的正式版Windows裝置。新模型參數量減少，卻能處理更長的輸入內容，並將擴大支援Nvidia RTX及AMD RDNA 4系列GPU。

items.title: refactor(agents): replace tool-loop detectors with an arguments-only …
items.summary: refactor(agents): replace tool-loop detectors with an arguments-only repeat guard (#199591) ## Problem The tool-loop guard was 12 files and about 1,700 lines. It hashed tool outcomes, had name checks for single tools (exec, message, wait, memory_search, computer, progress_card, write, process), and had four separate detectors plus a post-compaction guard. Rolling detection was opt-in, so most installs did not use it. One part was always on: after 3 identical failing calls, the next identical call ended the turn. The model got no chance to answer, and the user got a stop message in place of an answer. ## Fix One guard in `packages/agent-core/src/tool-repeat-guard.ts` (105 lines), used by the agent loop: - It compares each tool call with the call before it. It compares the tool name and the canonical arguments only. It never compares outcomes. - 3rd identical call in a row: the call runs, and a redirect note is added to its result. The note names the tool and tells the model to change its approach. - 20th identical call in a row: the call does not run. The turn ends with the typed reason `tool_repeat_limit` and this message: `OpenClaw stopped this turn: the model called with the same arguments 20 times in a row. Send a new message to continue.` - Tools declare `repeatable` themselves and skip the check: Code Mode `wait`, `process` poll/log/list, `agents_wait`, `sessions_yield`, `subagents` list/wait, `computer` screenshot/wait. The declaration is plain data (`true` or `{ actions: [...] }`), so it crosses the worker wire. - Worker turns (cloud and node workers) run the same guard over all their tools. The Gateway resolves `tools.loopDetection.enabled` (agent over global) into the worker tool-surface policy as `toolRepeatGuard`, and each tool definition carries its `repeatable` exemption. Two optional fields are added to the closed worker tool-surface schema (`definition.repeatable`, `policy.toolRepeatGuard`); worker bundles are build-bound to the Gateway. - Calls to an unknown tool are keyed by name. - New user input resets the streak. Removed: outcome hashing, per-tool checks, argument churn, ping-pong, the rolling history, batch admission and recovery state, the post-compaction guard, the "3 identical failures" hard stop and its error code. Repeated identical failing calls now get the same note and cap as any other repeat. Config: - `tools.loopDetection.enabled` stays. `false` turns the guard off. Unset or `true` keeps it on. This also folds the rolling detection that was opt-in into the one default rule. - The Codex `appServer.loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` key is retired. `openclaw doctor --fix` removes it. - The `tool.loop` diagnostic event stays, with `detector: "tool_repeat"`. ## User impact - A model that repeats a failing call now gets a note and can still answer, instead of the turn ending after 3 failures. - A model stuck on one call is stopped after 20 identical calls with a clear message, on local and worker turns alike. - `tools.loopDetection.enabled: false` still turns the guard off. Existing configs keep loading; `openclaw doctor --fix` removes the retired keys. ## Proof | Check | Tier | Base (`5d5ca9d2`) | Head (`ecb05477`) | |---|---|---|---| | Unit: note at 3rd identical call, stop at 20th with `tool_repeat_limit`, repeatable tools skip, unknown tool keyed by name, guard off when disabled (`tool-repeat-guard.test.ts`) | vitest-source | n/a (new) | 10/10 pass | | Regression: 4 identical failing calls, then the model answers | vitest-source | **fails**: turn ends after 3 failures, no answer | pass | | Real Gateway, mock model repeats one failing read (`tool-loop-global-breaker`, step 1) | dist-nodts | **fails**: Gateway logs `OpenClaw stopped this turn: the same read call failed 3 times`, run ends in error with no answer | pass: note on 3rd read, model recovers with its final answer | | Real Gateway, mock model ignores the note (step 2) | dist-nodts | n/a | pass: exactly 20 reads, 20th not run, user sees the `tool_repeat_limit` message | | Regression: worker turn with loop detection on, `progress_card` called 3 times with `{"markdown":"Still working"}` gets the redirect note on the 3rd result; with `tools.loopDetection.enabled: false` it gets none (`worker.runtime.test.ts`, real worker runtime + fake Gateway) | vitest-source | **fails** on `a3f26f46` (worker forced `enabled: false`) | pass | | Gateway policy: `toolRepeatGuard: false` only when loop detection is off; agent setting overrides global (`prepared-tool-surface.test.ts`) | vitest-source | n/a (new) | pass | | Upgrade: config written by latest stable `2026.11.3` (`tools.loopDetection.enabled`, Codex `appServer.loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` + `requestTimeoutMs`) plus the old sub-keys (`windowSize`, `historySize`, `warningThreshold`, `criticalThreshold`, `globalCircuitBreakerThreshold`, `detectors`, `postCompactionGuard`, which stable already rejects, as left by older releases); stable Gateway runs turn 1 on a mock model; head `openclaw doctor --fix`; head Gateway starts and runs turns 2 and 3 on the same session (fresh HOME, throwaway ports) | source CLI | | pass: doctor removes every retired key and keeps `enabled` and `requestTimeoutMs`; head Gateway starts on the migrated config; turn 2 answers; turn 3's provider request contains turn 1's reply, so the session survives | | `packages/agent-core` | vitest-source | | 29 files, 343 tests pass | | 51 touched unit test files + 2 before-tool-call e2e files | vitest-source | | pass | | `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` | type | | pass | | Full build with declarations + packed tarball check | full | | pass; guard in package, old symbols absent | | `rg` for every removed symbol across `src/ scripts/ test/ extensions/ packages/` | static | | 0 hits | ## Net lines `209 files changed, 1275 insertions(+), 9989 deletions(-)` (net -8,714) - Source: +815 / -3,585 (net -2,770; includes the regenerated `predicates.js` validator) - Tests: +391 / -6,198 (net -5,807) - Docs: +69 / -206 (net -137) Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: fix(control-ui): remove ellipses from chat progress labels (#198560)
items.summary: fix(control-ui): remove ellipses from chat progress labels (#198560) * feat(clawhub): let chat plugin cards represent community plugins The card payload reader required official: true, so a Gateway-authored card for a community plugin was dropped before it reached the chat. Plugin cards now carry the registry's official flag; skill cards stay official-only. The loading placeholder shows the official badge only for official cards. The loaded card already rechecks the Gateway's catalog answer, shows no badge for a community plugin, and offers View details instead of Install. * feat(message): show one exact ClawHub plugin card by package name clawhub now takes either query (search, unchanged) or plugin, the exact ClawHub package name. The exact form looks up that one package, never falls back to search, and shows its existing card. A name ClawHub does not know, or that is not a plugin, returns an explanation and shows no card. Search still returns official plugins and skills only. An exactly named community plugin is shown with the registry's own official flag. * docs(control-ui): document exact ClawHub plugin cards * fix(chat): render source reply cards before run adoption * test(chat): classify producer display regression as Node integration * fix(message): send ClawHub cards without generated captions * perf(chat): consolidate source reply admission and card decoding * test(chat): document independent card delivery proof boundaries * refactor(chat): use native named-export lazy card loading * refactor(outbound): keep attachment normalization in payload owner * test(chat): attach profile isolation reason to the mock * feat(templates): name the Template's agent in catalog detail The release detail already validates the Template's agent id from the ClawHub manifest summary. Return it so a client can name the agent it wants before Add, without a plan. * feat(templates): add a plan-free chat mode to templates.add.apply A request with mode "chat" names the agent id it wants and carries no plan digest. The Gateway admits the agent and chat under an unused id, fetches the Template, writes its workspace, then installs declared skills, bundled plugins and MCP servers one at a time. A dependency that cannot be set up is collected instead of stopping creation, and plugins referenced on ClawHub and automations are left to the agent's conversation. Failing to fetch the Template or write its workspace removes the agent and chat this request created. The agent's first turn starts after creation and receives a setup report through buildTemplateOpeningMessage, which still returns the existing opening. The plan-based request used by the CLI is unchanged. * feat(templates): copy CLAW.md and allow setup tools in chat-based Add Chat-based Add copies the Template's CLAW.md unchanged to the workspace root as an ordinary file, bound into the same retry checkpoint as the other workspace files. A Template whose own workspace files claim that path keeps its file and the setup report says so. The saved tool allowlist gains automations, plugins and message when the Template's allowlist omits them. A Template without an allowlist inherits the operator's policy, and a tool the Template denies stays denied. * test(templates): cover chat-based Add at the Gateway request seam Drive templates.add.apply in chat mode against a Template fixture shaped like Travel Copilot, with real admission, workspace, bundled skill and plugin, MCP and rollback owners. A declared plugin that is installed but disabled does not block, a missing skill keeps the agent and is reported, an unfetchable Template or failed workspace write leaves no agent, chat or workspace, and a taken id yields the next unused one. * feat(ui): add Templates from the Control UI without a plan Add no longer requests templates.add.plan. It sends one chat-mode templates.add.apply with the release's package name, exact version and an agent id derived from the Template's own id, then opens the pending chat as before. The review step for plugin capability grants and skill warnings is gone from the Add path; ClawHub's audit of a flagged release still asks first. A card Add reads the release detail once, because only the detail names the Template's agent. When the Gateway answers a first Add with an error it kept nothing, so the user returns to the catalog with the error on that card. * docs(templates): describe plan-free Add from the Control UI * fix(templates): retain effective setup tool grants in chat Add * fix(ui): open Template chat before resolving release details * fix(templates): reserve original manifest in chat Add * fix(templates): extract Gateway Add result leaf contract * perf(templates): keep trust decoder outside shared UI boot * fix(templates): report incomplete chat Add setup truthfully * test(templates): preserve reviewed checkpoint across chat retry refusal * fix(pr): include the ClawHub trust reader in wrapper extraction * perf(templates): decode trust errors without connection adapter * fix(templates): explain reserved manifest recovery after rollback * test(templates): reconcile creation regression allocation * feat(templates): add the setup prompt for a new Template agent The Gateway is moving to create a Template agent deterministically and leave the remaining setup to the agent's own first turn. This adds the hidden prompt for that turn. It is not used yet. The prompt fixes the order of the setup conversation: greeting, paused automations from CLAW.md, added MCP servers, ClawHub plugin state and install cards, creation failures, then the author's BOOTSTRAP.md opening. Automations carry the same declaration key, schedule, session target and delivery as the Gateway installer creates today, so a second run adds no duplicates. CLAW.md and the report are author-influenced, so the prompt treats them as data. Report text reaches the model only as bounded JSON, and two rules hold whatever a workspace file says: automations stay paused, and only the user installs or enables a plugin. * feat(gateway): run a Template setup prompt with the agent's tools The Template opening turn passed an empty runtime tool allowlist, which removes every tool, so the agent could not finish its own setup. startAgentOnboardingConversation now accepts the setup prompt for a Template agent. With one, the turn sends that prompt and passes no runtime allowlist, so the agent's own tool policy decides what it can call. The prompt stays hidden from the chat as before. No caller passes a prompt yet, so the existing Template opening and New agent onboarding still run without tools. * fix(plugins): preserve exact package identity in tool inventory * feat(templates): finish Add through retryable hidden setup * docs(templates): reconcile chat Add manifest and heartbeat limits * fix(templates): present setup cards without redundant narration * fix(templates): preserve incomplete dependency results through setup retry * fix(templates): keep setup retry outcomes truthful independently * fix(templates): attach chat while dependency setup settles * test(chat): provide submission owners to chat fixtures * docs(templates): cite concurrent setup prompt incident * fix(templates): keep Add timing diagnostics at debug level * test(ui): supply submissions owner to plugin identity fixture * fix(ui): retain Template Retry input across reconnects * test(ui): share Template live-custody scenarios * fix(control-ui): remove ellipses from chat progress labels * test(ui): preserve connection settings reconnect label * test(ui): align live activity expectations with status copy * test(ui): align remaining e2e progress expectations with status copy The command palette preview, tool-turn outcome and Mantis chat proof scenarios still expected a trailing ellipsis on labels this change makes plain (Starting, Working, and the running activity headline).
